Experimental design

Experimental methodology

How the weight edits, instruction-following scores and browser resource measurements were obtained.

The research question

Ask Astra to modify the weights of a small language model with an explicit benchmark objective. Measure quality and runtime behavior, then inspect whether any improvement survives a fair comparison.

Base model
Qwen3.5-0.8B
Deployment
WebLLM 0.2.86 · q4f16_1
Quality benchmark
IFEval instruction following
Resource workload
Browser LLM Bench · standard
V1

Historical edit and held-out evaluation

A manually supplied edit was selected on 32 development prompts, then evaluated against the original on 128 held-out prompts. Strict prompt passes changed from 69 to 70. The paired 95% confidence interval crosses zero.

The candidate run was interrupted and resumed. Its token and timing observations do not establish a controlled resource improvement.

Inconclusive
V2

Fresh Astra proposals, bounded selection

Three fresh-context gpt-6-astra proposals were evaluated on the same 32 development prompts. Qualification required more than 16 strict passes, at most 13,941 output tokens, and valid deployment and memory limits. None qualified.

The saved baseline used Chrome 156; candidates used Chrome 157. No verified untouched final prompts remained. The conditional resource comparison was skipped.

Pristine retained
R

Independent all-artifact resource study

The follow-up protocol compares pristine, V1 and all three V2 edits on the original standard workload. Its mirrored order balances two sessions per artifact; eligibility in the earlier quality study is not required.

10 of 10 planned sessions are complete in the public report. Quality eligibility was not required. Two sessions per artifact form a descriptive pilot, not an equivalence test.

All-edit resource pilot

How do pristine and every completed edit compare on the same current browser resource workload?

Scope. Five artifacts × two browser sessions; 60 fixed-prompt measured requests per session. Quality qualification is not required. See the separate result for actual completion status.

Selection. Include all five frozen deployed artifacts regardless of development quality; do not select retrospectively from resource outcomes.

Aggregation. Compute each metric within each session first, then report both values and their equal-weight arithmetic mean/minimum/maximum. Artifact throughput is the mean of the two session throughput ratios, not pooled tokens divided by pooled seconds. Independently averaged throughput and milliseconds per token need not be reciprocals.

Public resource workload prompt. “In three short sentences, explain why leaves change color in autumn.”

Telemetry definitions and coverage
Sampled output tokens · tokens
Sum across measured requests; excludes warm-up and four injected boundary IDs. Measured completions Different output lengths mean different realized work. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Total response time · ms
Sum of browser wall time around measured completion calls, including prefill and decode. Measured requests Excludes load, warm-up and idle gaps; not full-session or decode-only time. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Response time per sampled token · ms/token
Within each session: summed response milliseconds divided by sampled output tokens. Across sessions: equal-weight mean of the two session values; it need not be the inverse of mean throughput. Session ratio of sums Includes prefill overhead; output-length differences affect normalization. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Model load time · ms
Reported model load duration. One load Separate from warm-up and session timing; browser cache policy does not guarantee a cold operating-system cache. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Profile session time · ms
Total measured profile duration, including prescribed baseline, idle and recovery phases. Browser profile Separate from response time and controller-stage ledger time. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Peak accounted process footprint · decimal GB
Maximum sampled sum of per-process ri_phys_footprint during the profile, divided by 1e9. Dedicated Chrome process tree Not globally deduplicated physical RAM; do not add GPU descriptors, WASM address space or RSS. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Final loaded-idle footprint · decimal GB
Median sampled footprint in the idle phase after the final active window. Dedicated Chrome process tree A retained-memory observation, not all machine memory. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Recovery footprint · decimal GB
Median sampled footprint during recovery. Dedicated Chrome process tree A remaining level, not the amount of memory freed. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
CPU capacity · %
Time-weighted complete process-tree CPU intervals divided by logical CPU count. Dedicated Chrome process tree Valid, wholly contained active-interval duration divided by total active duration 100% means total logical CPU capacity under this normalization, not one core. This is an activity rate, not cumulative computation; a lower rate with a longer response does not establish less total work. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Experimental GPU time · ms/s
Driver-accounted command-buffer time per elapsed second via AGX AppUsage. Dedicated Chrome process tree, including rendering Valid, wholly contained active-interval duration divided by total active duration Not GPU utilization, occupancy, arithmetic-operation count or model-only time; queues may overlap and counter changes invalidate intervals. This is a rate: lower GPU milliseconds per second with a longer response does not establish less cumulative work. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
GPU buffer descriptors · bytes
Sampled maximum of WebGPU buffer descriptor byte accounting. WebGPU allocation bookkeeping Not physical VRAM or residency. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
WASM address space · bytes
Sampled maximum of WebAssembly linear-memory byte length. WASM linear address space Not physical residency; do not add to native footprint. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Host subsystem power · W
Observed CPU/GPU/ANE subsystem estimate, interval-weighted over valid active intervals. Whole-host subsystems Valid, wholly contained active-interval duration divided by total active duration Not wall power or model watts; unprivileged capture may leave it unavailable. Watts are a rate, not energy: lower power with longer duration does not establish lower joules. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Host subsystem energy · J
Original merger integrates observed power-interval overlap across first-active to last-active bounds; may include between-burst idle. Whole-host subsystems Original observed covered-interval duration; missing intervals are not filled Not request-only energy or causal model energy; five-second observed pre-run baseline where available. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Mean response time · ms/request
Summed measured response time divided by measured request count. Session A mean within a session does not add independent experimental replicates. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
End-to-end output throughput · tokens/s
Within each session: summed measured output tokens divided by summed response seconds. Across two sessions: equal-weight arithmetic mean of those two ratios, not a pooled token/second ratio. Session ratio of sums Not a mean of request rates, decode-only throughput or equal work when lengths differ. Unavailable/null, never zero-filled
Reproduction and preserved failures
  • Use pinned source model/data revisions and released ordered item IDs; selection reruns without private exclusions may differ.
  • Reconstruct each independent deterministic source transformation and verify complete source/deployment manifest identities.
  • Verify current environment, actual fetched model/runtime bytes, per-session manifests and durable accounting before interpreting resource differences.
  • Public hashes and aggregates support reconstruction and arithmetic audits; withheld raw outputs and private custody records are needed for independent original regrading and editor-access verification.
  • V1 conversion-environment failure and the 94+34 manually continued candidate final evaluation remain documented.
  • V2 initial sandbox failure generated nothing but consumed one browser attempt; only three real candidate evaluations remained.
  • V2 round 3 offline grading stopped before any checker call after completed browser output and cleanup. Exact-byte recovery and one 27.657-second offline pass added zero model loads/generations or editor calls. Nineteen harness files, 171 pinned evaluator payloads and four frozen inputs were recovered; 347 unavailable bytecodes were quarantined; the 758/758 frozen-input preflight matched.
  • The all-artifact resource study stopped after six completed sessions when the position-7 integrity check timed out on an offloaded protected historical file. The failed check charged 28.943 seconds, with no session-7 reservation, model load or generation. The original 10,135 bytes were later ordinarily materialized with the exact frozen hash and no overwrite. A separate continuation is limited to original positions 7–10 under the retained clocks and deadline. The slow second R3 observation and the inter-session gap remain part of the evidence; no uninterrupted run is claimed.

Fresh six-version study

Recorded progress. 6 of 6 quality evaluations and 12 of 12 resource sessions are complete. The report status is complete.

Pristine, V1 and the three prior Astra edits are evaluated first on the same 32 development prompts. A fresh-context Astra agent receives the approved weight information and all five fresh development results before proposing one fourth edit. The new edit starts from pristine and scales one contiguous 60-column block in each of layers 15 and 19, with an independent multiplier chosen from 0.5, 0.75, 1.25 and 1.5. Tensor shapes, tokenizer, grading and decoding rules stay fixed.

The primary target is higher strict compliance than both fresh pristine and the best fresh prior edit. Equal or fewer output tokens is a secondary target, not evidence of equal compute. Every technically valid version proceeds to resource measurement regardless of its quality score; quality gains and cost changes are reported separately.

Astra round 4 · pre-evaluation hypothesis

The following decision summary was saved and hashed with the proposal before the new weights were built or evaluated. It records a prediction, not an explanation established by the eventual score.

Intervention: R4 stronger V1-support attenuation. From pristine, scale columns 0–59 of both layer 15 and layer 19 MLP down-projection weights by 0.5. This tests a stronger dose on the only support with a fresh net strict-compliance gain; the other tested supports changed length without improving aggregate compliance. I predict a small chance of exceeding 17/32, with 16–18/32 a plausible central range, rather than a dependable improvement. V1's extra pass came from repetitive highlighting, so it is weak evidence of genuine instruction-following improvement. The intended effect is improved constraint adherence while preserving existing passes, not inducing repetition. Output tokens may remain near pristine or decline, but could rise. I expect essentially unchanged allocation sizes and no reliable per-token resource improvement; cumulative work depends on generated length. These are uncertain predictions on exposed development data, with no neuron-semantic claim or generalization evidence.

One fresh-context collaboration agent was requested with the gpt-6-astra selector. It received the approved weight packet and five fresh development evaluations. Provider-side immutable model identity, accepted effort, token usage and billing are unavailable; browser inference measurements below do not include the editor’s compute.

The resource schedule runs pristine, V1, Astra rounds 1–4, then reverses that order. Each of the twelve sessions includes one warm-up and 60 measured fixed-prompt requests. The browser session is the replication unit. The mirrored schedule is deterministic, not randomized, and cannot eliminate nonlinear drift or background activity.

Recorded environment matching. Quality: verified. Resources: verified. Matching runtime identities does not prove constant host conditions. The actual observations, failures, completion status and accounting are preserved in the downloadable report.

This adaptive development comparison supplies no untouched final-quality evaluation. Higher development scores are not a generalization claim. CPU/GPU rates and footprint are measured within their stated scopes; no FLOP count, causal energy saving or resource equivalence is inferred.

Frozen limits and accounting

The schedule permits 18 model loads, 18 warm-ups, 192 quality requests and 720 resource requests. The 930 total dispatches reserve at most 242,976 output positions, including control positions; this is a capacity ceiling, not observed model output.

One editor proposal, response import, source build, conversion and package are allowed. Automatic retries are zero. Browser time is capped at 180 minutes, charged local time at 240 minutes and calendar time at 24 hours. Failed preparation, integrity checks, grading and reporting consume the local allowance. Reservations, actual usage and cleanup status are retained separately in the report.

Preparation and provenance

All preparation used zero target-model calls. Exact source bytes and deployed artifacts were verified before the first model load.

The converter was reconstructed from 75 same-version cached wheels. Wheel RECORD digests and available installed RECORD digests were checked; 27 historical installed RECORDs were unavailable, so full old-environment byte equality is not claimed.

Ten new local library copies received signature-only ad-hoc signing, with unchanged code/data payloads verified; three readable historical signed libraries matched byte for byte.

The 435-parameter metadata was extracted from the unchanged, verified compiled WASM; equality to the unavailable historical JSON bytes is not claimed.

Preparation rejected 73 extra language files in the new tokenizer staging and a converter executable symlink. The English-only allowlist and explicit interpreter selector/binary/config binding were corrected before freezing; original inputs were preserved.

Earlier console-script and signature-metadata preparation failures were preserved. All failed preparation and accounting amendments are included in conservative local elapsed-time charges.

What would support a stronger claim?

A stronger quality claim needs evaluation on verified untouched tasks. Resource conclusions need more repeated sessions, randomized ordering and independent repeats across devices. The workload and counter scopes must remain explicit.

Built on open work

Browser LLM Bench by Gufran Mirza and Arhaan Aggarwal supplies the resource workload. Instruction-following evaluation builds on Google’s IFEval and the Ai2 RLVR-IFeval development data.

Model: Qwen. Browser runtime: WebLLM / MLC. The repository records the underlying weight-space research and experiment history.

How to read this record

This is an experimental research record, not a peer-reviewed result. Development performance, held-out quality, and resource measurements are separate evidence scopes. Missing observations remain unavailable.
